questions.q: What is the term for the amount of heat that is absorbed or evolved when a substance changes its state without changing its temperature?
questions.n: Latent heat is the energy released or absorbed during a phase change (like ice melting to water) while the temperature remains constant.

questions.q: In a septic tank, what is the required minimum width and minimum liquid depth?
questions.n: According to standard utility codes, a septic tank must be at least 90 cms wide with a liquid depth of at least 60 cms.

questions.q: What is the minimum distance required between a water supply well and a septic tank?
questions.n: Building codes specify 15.20 meters as the minimum safe buffer to protect water wells from septic contamination.

questions.q: Which gauge of galvanized sheet is standard for use in downspouts?
questions.n: Gauge 26 is the standard thickness specified for galvanized sheets used in downspout construction.

questions.q: In wire specifications, what does the abbreviation 'THHN' stand for?
questions.n: This specific technical definition corresponds to high-performance wiring used in demanding environments.

questions.q: What is the minimum elevator width for a single slide door elevator in a small commercial or residential building?
questions.n: For small residential or commercial applications, 0.60 meters is the minimum designated width for this elevator type.

questions.q: What device is used to automatically transfer power from a standby generator to a building's circuitry during a power failure?
questions.n: An ATS detects power loss and automatically switches the load to the backup generator to ensure continuity.

questions.q: What is the standard length of an electrical metal conduit?
questions.n: The industry standard for the length of an electrical metal conduit (EMC) is 10 feet.

questions.q: What is the standard size of wire used for a circuit line?
questions.n: No. 12 AWG is the standard wire size for most general-purpose circuit lines in building wiring.

questions.q: A controller that is sensitive to the degree of moisture in the air is called a:
questions.n: A humidistat (also known as a hygrostat) regulates equipment based on the humidity levels in the air.

questions.q: What is the minimum length required for a septic tank?
questions.n: Standard regulations require a minimum longitudinal dimension of 1.50 meters to allow for proper settlement.

questions.q: What is the maximum liquid depth allowed for a septic tank?
questions.n: To maintain efficient anaerobic digestion and prevent excessive turbulence, the depth is capped at 1.80 meters.

questions.q: For a septic tank with a capacity greater than 6 cubic meters, what is the minimum length of the secondary compartment?
questions.n: Larger systems require a secondary compartment of at least 1.50 meters to ensure final clarification of effluent.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension required for a manhole access to a septic tank?
questions.n: A 508 mm opening is the standard minimum to allow for inspection and pumping equipment.

questions.q: What is the minimum distance required between a water supply well and a disposal field?
questions.n: Disposal fields require a 30.50-meter buffer to protect the well from leaching contaminants.

questions.q: What is the minimum distance required between a water supply well and a seepage pit or cesspool?
questions.n: Due to the depth and concentration of waste, a seepage pit requires the largest buffer at 45.70 meters.

questions.q: What are the minimum and maximum heights for a water seal in each fixture trap?
questions.n: The trap must maintain a seal between 51 mm and 102 mm to prevent sewer gases from entering the building.

questions.q: What is the maximum length allowed for the tailpiece from any fixture?
questions.n: A tailpiece is limited to 60 cms to prevent high-velocity discharge from siphoning the trap seal.

questions.q: What is the minimum extension of the VSTR (Vent Stack Through Roof) above the roofline?
questions.n: Vents must extend at least 15 cms above the roof to ensure gases are dispersed safely.

questions.q: What is the minimum extension of a VSTR above an openable window, door opening, or air intake?
questions.n: A 0.90-meter clearance is required to ensure gas does not drift into building apertures.

questions.q: What are the minimum trap diameters for a bathtub and a shower stall, respectively?
questions.n: Bathtubs require a 38 mm trap, while shower stalls require 51 mm due to drainage volume.

questions.q: How many water closets are required for females in an auditorium serving 16-35 people?
questions.n: For an auditorium with 16-35 people, the code specifies 3 water closets for females.

questions.q: How many water closets are required for males in an auditorium serving 16-35 people?
questions.n: Auditorium standards require 2 water closets for males when serving 16-35 people.

questions.q: In an auditorium serving 10-50 people, what is the required number of urinals?
questions.n: Code specifies 1 urinal for every 10-50 occupants in an auditorium setting.

questions.q: How many water closets are required for females for a theater serving 51-100 people?
questions.n: Theater settings for 51-100 females require 4 water closets to manage higher peak traffic.

questions.q: What are the two classifications of copper pipes mentioned in the standards?
questions.n: Copper piping is technically classified as either Rigid (hard-drawn) or Flexible (annealed).

questions.q: What is the technical term for a rough or sharp edge left on metal by a cutting tool?
questions.n: A burr is the unwanted edge or ridge of metal left after a cutting or drilling operation.

questions.q: What are the two types of passenger elevators listed?
questions.n: Passenger elevators are categorized based on their drive system: Electric (traction) or Hydraulic.

questions.q: What does 'TW' in electrical wire specifications mean?
o: Moisture resistant, in wet and dry location
questions.n: TW indicates a thermoplastic insulation that is moisture resistant for use in both wet and dry areas.

questions.q: What is another name for a passenger elevator?
questions.n: 'Lift' is the standard alternative term used for a passenger elevator.

questions.q: What is the minimum face-to-face distance between elevators in a three or four-car grouping?
questions.n: Multi-car groupings require a 2-meter clearance between opposing elevator doors for traffic flow.

questions.q: The collection line of a plumbing system is sometimes referred to as the:
questions.n: The House Drain is the horizontal pipe that receives the discharge from all soil and waste stacks.

questions.q: What is the maximum height of a dumbwaiter?
questions.n: To be classified as a dumbwaiter rather than a freight elevator, the height is capped at 1.20 meters.

questions.q: What type of lighting provides illumination to special objects like sculptures or flower arrangements?
questions.n: Specific (or accent) lighting is designed to highlight particular features or objects.

questions.q: What is an assembly consisting of a pulley wheel, side plates, shaft, and bearings over which a cable or rope is passed?
questions.n: A sheave is the technical term for the pulley wheel assembly used in elevator systems.

questions.q: Other than the ultraviolet type, what is the other type of flame detector?
questions.n: Flame detectors typically sense either UV or Infra Red (IR) radiation from a fire.

questions.q: What does PABX or PBX stand for?
questions.n: PBX stands for Private Branch Exchange, and PABX adds 'Automatic' to the designation.

questions.q: Farad is the unit capacity of a _______.
questions.n: Capacitance, the ability to store an electrical charge, is measured in Farads.

questions.q: What is another name for a distribution panel?
questions.n: A distribution panel is frequently referred to as a Power Panel in utility documentation.

questions.q: Which type of plastic pipe is listed as an alternative to polyvinyl chloride and polybutylene?
questions.n: Polyethylene (PE) is listed alongside PVC and polybutylene as a standard plastic piping material.

questions.q: What is the standard size of wire used for a switch line?
questions.n: No. 14 is the standard wire size for lighting switch lines in residential wiring.

questions.q: What device is used for converting alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC)?
questions.n: A rectifier is the specific electrical device that allows current to flow in one direction only, converting AC to DC.

questions.q: What is another name for a Rectifier?
questions.n: Because it produces direct current, a rectifier is sometimes referred to as a D.C. Generator.

questions.q: What is another name for a Humidistat?
questions.n: Hygrostat is the technical synonym for a humidistat, both measuring air moisture.

questions.q: What is the minimum capacity (in cubic meters) required for the secondary compartment of a septic tank?
questions.n: Building codes require the secondary compartment to have a minimum volume of 1 cubic meter.

questions.q: True or False: A Lawn Sprinkler System is a system of devices installed below ground to scatter water droplets over a lawn or golf course.
questions.n: This accurately defines the function and standard installation of a lawn sprinkler system.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a septic tank?
questions.n: The minimum width to ensure proper flow and volume in a septic tank is 90 cms.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the material constraints for septic tanks?
o: Wooden septic tanks are NOT allowed
questions.n: Per standard sanitation codes, septic tanks must be made of durable, non-decaying materials like concrete.

questions.q: What is the maximum height of a water seal for each fixture trap?
questions.n: The depth of the trap seal must not exceed 102 mm to ensure proper scouring during flush.

questions.q: What is the standard length of an electrical metal conduit?
questions.n: Electrical conduit is manufactured in standard 10-foot sections.

questions.q: In wire specifications, what does XHHN represent?
questions.n: XHHN indicates a highly durable, cross-linked thermoset insulation designed for extreme conditions.

questions.q: What is the minimum liquid depth for a septic tank?
questions.n: A depth of 60 cms is the absolute minimum to allow for sludge and scum layers.

questions.q: A device that transfers power from a standby generator to a building circuitry during a failure is an:
questions.n: The ATS is the critical component that bridges the building to emergency power sources.

questions.q: What is the minimum elevator width of a single slide door elevator for a small commercial or residential building?
questions.n: The code allows a minimum of 0.60 meters for small-scale installations.

questions.q: What is the minimum extension of a VSTR above the roof?
questions.n: The 15 cms minimum ensures the vent remains clear and functional.

questions.q: How many water closets are required for males in an auditorium serving 16-35 people?
questions.n: Two water closets are mandated for males in this specific occupancy range.

questions.q: What is the term for a controller sensitive to moisture in the air?
questions.n: Humidistats are the standard device for maintaining set humidity levels.

questions.q: What is the standard size of wire for a circuit line?
questions.n: No. 12 AWG is the industry standard for most building circuit lines.

questions.q: What is the required number of urinals for an auditorium serving 10-50 people?
questions.n: For this population size, a single urinal is the minimum requirement.

questions.q: Which gauge of galvanized sheet is used for downspouts?
questions.n: Gauge 26 is the specific industry standard for durable galvanized downspouts.
